content: 1. Famotidine reduces the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH, which decreases the solubility of ledipasvir. H2-receptor antagonists like famotidine can be administered either simultaneously or 12 hours apart from ledipasvir/sofosbuvir, at doses not exceeding famotidine 40 mg twice daily. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Fostamatinib increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing concentrations of P-gp/BCRP substrate drugs. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp/BCRP substrates, and consider dosage reduction when co-administered with fostamatinib. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Fostemsavir increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Avoid co-administration if possible, or modify the dose of BCRP substrates co-administered with fostemsavir. Monitor closely. 4. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Conversely, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing plasma concentrations of P-gp and BCRP substrates. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Ibuprofen/famotidine reduces the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH, which decreases the solubility of ledipasvir. H2-receptor antagonists like famotidine can be administered either simultaneously or 12 hours apart from ledipasvir/sofosbuvir, at doses not exceeding famotidine 40 mg twice daily. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Clinical trials have shown that istradefylline 40 mg/day increases peak levels and AUC of P-gp substrates. Consider dose reduction of sensitive P-gp substrates. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Lansoprazole reduces the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH, which decreases the solubility of ledipasvir. Proton-pump inhibitor doses comparable to omeprazole <20 mg can be administered simultaneously with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir under fasted conditions. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Lonafarnib increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Lonafarnib is a weak P-gp inhibitor. Monitor for adverse reactions if co-administered with P-gp substrates, as minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. Reduce P-gp substrate dose if needed. Monitor closely. 9. Magnesium oxide reduces the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH, which decreases the solubility of ledipasvir. Separate antacid and ledipasvir/sofosbuvir administration by 4 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Mavorixafor, a P-gp inhibitor, may increase the systemic exposure of sensitive P-gp substrates, leading to serious adverse effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Momelotinib increases the toxicity of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by plasma protein binding competition. Momelotinib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase exposure to BCRP substrates, raising the risk of adverse reactions. Dose adjustment of other BCRP substrates may be necessary. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 12. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases the levels of naldemedine via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor naldemedine for potential adverse effects if co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases the levels of nintedanib via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. If adverse effects occur, management may require interruption, dose reduction, or discontinuation of therapy. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 14. Nizatidine reduces the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH, which decreases the solubility of ledipasvir. H2-receptor antagonists like nizatidine can be administered either simultaneously or 12 hours apart from ledipasvir/sofosbuvir, at doses not exceeding famotidine 40 mg twice daily. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Omeprazole reduces the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH, which decreases the solubility of ledipasvir. Proton-pump inhibitor doses comparable to omeprazole <20 mg can be administered simultaneously with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir under fasted conditions. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Otesaconazole increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by inhibiting BCRP transporters. This may increase the effects and risk of toxicities of BCRP substrates. Use the lowest starting dose of BCRP substrates or consider reducing their dose. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 17. Pantoprazole reduces the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH, which decreases the solubility of ledipasvir. Proton-pump inhibitor doses comparable to omeprazole <20 mg can be administered simultaneously with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir under fasted conditions. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Rabeprazole reduces the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH, which decreases the solubility of ledipasvir. Proton-pump inhibitor doses comparable to omeprazole <20 mg can be administered simultaneously with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir under fasted conditions. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Regorafenib increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by likely inhibiting BCRP (ABCG2) transport. Co-administration with a BCRP substrate may increase systemic exposure to the substrate and related toxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 20. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases the levels or effects of rosuvastatin by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Co-administration may increase the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. Monitor closely. 21. Safinamide increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by inhibiting intestinal BCRP. Monitor BCRP substrates for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Sarecycline increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrates, and consider dosage reduction when co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases the levels of seladelpar. Monitor seladelpar for adverse effects if co-administered with BCRP inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate reduces the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral form of both agents. Administer drugs at least 2 hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 25. Stiripentol increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and by inhibiting BCRP transport. Consider dosage reduction for BCRP substrates if adverse effects occur when co-administered. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 26. Tafamidis increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by inhibiting breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) in vitro. This may increase exposure to BCRP substrates following tafamidis or tafamidis meglumine administration. Dosage adjustment of these BCRP substrates may be necessary. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases the levels or effects of talazoparib via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Talazoparib is a P-gp substrate, and co-administration with P-gp inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates, where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Vadadustat increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing exposure to BCRP substrates. Monitor for signs of adverse effects of BCRP substrates and reduce substrate dose in accordance with their product labeling. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Acalabrutinib increases the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by inhibiting intestinal BCRP. Monitor closely for increased exposure to co-administered BCRP substrates. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH, which decreases the solubility of ledipasvir. Separate antacid and ledipasvir/sofosbuvir administration by 4 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH, which decreases the solubility of ledipasvir. Separate antacid and ledipasvir/sofosbuvir administration by 4 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate reduces the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH, which decreases the solubility of ledipasvir. Separate antacid and ledipasvir/sofosbuvir administration by 4 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases the toxicity of amiodarone by an unknown mechanism. Postmarketing reports describe bradycardia resulting in death or pacemaker insertion when amiodarone was co-administered with sofosbuvir in combination with another direct-acting antiviral. Patients also taking beta blockers or those with underlying cardiac comorbidities and/or advanced liver disease may be at increased risk for symptomatic bradycardia. Cardiac monitoring in an inpatient setting for the first 48 hours of co-administration is recommended, followed by outpatient or self-monitoring of heart rate daily for at least the first 2 weeks of treatment. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 36. Apalutamide reduces the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing elimination. Apalutamide weakly induces BCRP and may decrease systemic exposure of drugs that are BCRP substrates. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH, which decreases the solubility of ledipasvir. Separate antacid and ledipasvir/sofosbuvir administration by 4 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases the levels or effects of atorvastatin by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Co-administration may increase the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. Monitor closely. 39. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases the levels of berotralstat via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Berotralstat also increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir via the same mechanism. Monitor or titrate P-gp substrate dose if co-administered. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases the levels of betrixaban via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Decrease betrixaban dose to 80 mg orally once, then 40 mg orally daily if co-administered with a P-gp inhibitor. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Calcium carbonate reduces the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH, which decreases the solubility of ledipasvir. Separate antacid and ledipasvir/sofosbuvir administration by 4 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Carbamazepine reduces the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. P-gp inducers decrease sofosbuvir levels, reducing conversion to its active metabolite (GS-331007), which is responsible for 90% of its pharmacologic effect. Co-administration is contraindicated. 43. Cimetidine reduces the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH, which decreases the solubility of ledipasvir. H2-receptor antagonists like cimetidine can be administered either simultaneously or 12 hours apart from ledipasvir/sofosbuvir, at doses not exceeding famotidine 40 mg twice daily. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH, which decreases the solubility of ledipasvir. Separate antacid and ledipasvir/sofosbuvir administration by 4 hours. Use caution and monitor closely.
